Thanks Laura — quick notes from my side:

Role scope update (short):
- Core: owning inference stack for multi-tenant hosted and dedicated deployments. Focus on throughput, KV cache strategies, graceful fallback across model variants.
- Expectation: Candidate should be able to design for 10k+ concurrent requests at 99th pctl SLOs, and propose concrete caching/batching approaches.
- Leveling: hiring at Senior Staff / early Principal. For us to move forward I want to see:
  * Design clarity for tradeoffs under cost/latency constraints
  * Practical experience shipping optimizations (quantization/engine-level changes or scheduler-level improvements)
  * Ownership signal: led rollouts or major infra migrations

For interviews:
- I'll take systems design slot and will emphasize end-to-end ownership, rollout plan, and measurable outcomes (give them a real product constraint).
- Marissa, please own implementation/debugging slot + a short coding task focused on diagnosing perf regressions from log traces.
- Vanessa, please treat the bar-raiser probe as the canonical tie-breaker — focus on open design questions, blind spots, and whether candidate can generalize tradeoffs.

I don't think we need a sync if everyone confirms. Dylan — please draft the interview plan and include the debrief rubric (pass/weak/pass/fail anchors). Mark timezones in invites.

Karthik

Thanks — quick calibration from me as bar-raiser:

Bar expectations (short anchors):
- PASS: Candidate proposes a clear, reasoned architecture with specific mitigations for tail latency; can cite measurable improvements from prior work; can walk tradeoffs with cost numbers.
- WEAK PASS: Good ideas but missing concrete measurements or rollout/rollback plan.
- FAIL: Can't articulate practical mitigations for production jitter/latency or only provides academic-level answers.

Focus areas I'd like interviewers to score and bring to debrief:
- Latency tail mitigation (SLA-driven design)
- Caching & batching strategies and KV cache invalidation edge cases
- Quantization and model-compat concerns (how they'd validate quality regressions)
- Cross-team communication: describing a past rollout where they aligned infra, ops, and product

I can run a 15-minute bar-raiser pre-loop sync at 3:30 PT if helpful. Also attaching the latest llm_serving_rubric_v2.xlsx — please use those anchors in the debrief (I've annotated critical fields).

V.

Thanks everyone — I put together interview_plan_JL_2345.docx (attached) and a short candidate briefing we will paste into invites. Key notes included:
- Keep the design prompt constrained: assume a hosted runtime (multi-tenant) with a 2K qps steady-state, spikes to 10K qps, and 95%/99%/99.9% latency targets. Ask candidate for rollout plan and post-deploy observability signals.
- Implementation slot: give an hour-long trace (synthetic) with an injected KV cache miss pattern; ask candidate to identify root cause and propose mitigations.
- Bar-raiser probe: two open-ended scenarios (model fallback when quantized variant degrades quality; cross-region model routing under capacity limits).

Scheduling: I created tentative slots and invited candidate + Catalyst (Sarah). Jia confirmed availability for 6/1 & 6/2 windows in the invite thread. Please accept the invites you own.

Debrief flow to follow in calendar invite: each interviewer fills the quick rubric (link in related_links) before the immediate 15-min debrief. If any interviewer marks FAIL or RED FLAG, we escalate to a 30-min sync.

Attachments: interview_plan_JL_2345.docx (contains time breakdown, question seeds, and debrief rubric link).

Cheers,

Looks good — accepted the slots. Two practical notes from the implementation slot perspective:

1) Keep the debugging trace focused on one dominant signal (e.g., a KV cache invalidation storm). We want the candidate to talk through instrumentation, hypothesis testing, and quick mitigations (config change / circuit-breaker / prioritization) rather than re-architecting.
2) Please flag the behavioral question in the invites: ask candidate to describe a time they had to push back on product to avoid reliability regressions. That will surface stakeholder influence.

If anyone is unsure about question wording I can draft a 2–3 sentence seed question to paste into the invites.

See you at the loop — Marissa
